For catalogue size N and k negatives/positive, α=k/(N−1), β=α[t(1−1/α)+1/α]=1−t+tα. Thus t=0 gives BCE; t=1 gives β=α, theoretically full calibration; authors recommend k=256,t=0.75. Transform only positive logits: γ(s)=−log(σ(s)^(−β)−1); negatives stay unchanged. Apply BCEWithLogits, average across k+1 candidates, then average over valid sequence positions. Equivalent exact loss: [β·softplus(−s⁺)+Σⱼsoftplus(sⱼ⁻)]/(k+1). Averaging positive and negative losses separately changes their relative weighting. [Official training code](https://github.com/asash/gSASRec-pytorch/blob/main/train_gsasrec.py).

Official transformation uses float64, ε=1e−10, clamps sigmoid to [ε,1−ε], inverse-power output to [1+ε,float64_max], and reciprocal to [ε,float64_max], then logs. Algebraic implementation recommendation: use the direct softplus loss above, avoiding sigmoid saturation, power overflow and subtractive cancellation; compute β as 1−t+tα. The positive transformation is for training; inference uses original scores. [Official implementation](https://github.com/asash/gSASRec-pytorch).

The calibration theorem explicitly assumes uniform sampling **with replacement** from items other than the current target: duplicates count toward k, so α uses draw count, not unique-count inclusion probability. However, the official PyTorch sampler uses unrestricted catalogue-wide randint, allowing target collisions and previously interacted items—a discrepancy from the theorem. Excluding every known training positive further changes sampling support: α=k/(N−|Hᵤ|) describes expected counts on eligible items, but merely substituting this denominator does not restore the theorem’s full-catalogue guarantee; excluded items receive no negative pressure. This is an inference from the proof, not a published guarantee for that sampler. [Paper, Theorem 5.1](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2308.07192), [official sampler](https://github.com/asash/gSASRec-pytorch/blob/main/dataset_utils.py).
